utterances.text: According to the information we received, in addition to Mr. Milosevic, the meeting was attended by the then head of public security, Mr. Vlastimir Djordjevic, General, and General Radomir Markovic, the then Minister Vlajko Stojiljkovic, and some other persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Very briefly, please, Mr. Karleusa. What was the subject of that meeting as far as information --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KARLEUSA
utterances.text: The need was discussed to conduct a clearing operation, as it were called, and also to eliminate any trace of anything that may fall within the interest of The Hague Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Did the working group make this information that came into its possession available to the public?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KARLEUSA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it did make it available to the public through a press conference.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And was that set out also in one of the communiques prepared by the working group?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KARLEUSA
utterances.text: That is precisely what I've said. What we found out we made public in our press release.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Your Honours, just in the interests of moving quickly here, I refer you to tab 3. In the English that's page 4, the second full paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Karleusa, I'd like to move on, actually. Mr. Karleusa, where did the working group learn at that March 1999 meeting? What was the setting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KARLEUSA
utterances.text: Towards the end of into 2001, I attended a meeting where I reported on the proceedings of the investigation related to the refrigerator truck when I was informed about the statement made by Mr. Radomir Markovic. That is to say that he said this in his statement, and that is roughly what we conveyed in our press release.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: When you say "statement made by Radomir Markovic," to whom did he make that statement as far as you understood?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KARLEUSA
utterances.text: He made this statement to the members of the State Security Service that discussed this matter with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And when you say you attended a meeting where you learned about this, what type of meeting was it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KARLEUSA
utterances.text: It was a regular meeting where I also provided information as to how far the investigation related to the refrigerator truck had gone.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Who are what types of people were present at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KARLEUSA
utterances.text: The leadership of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Karleusa, turning to the second meeting -- I'm sorry, the second meeting of the three I mentioned earlier. When did that meeting take place?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KARLEUSA
utterances.text: That meeting took place immediately after the first one we referred to, in the office of Mr. Vlajko Stojiljkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Who else was present according to the information available to the working group at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KARLEUSA
utterances.text: According to the information given by the same source, just like the previous one, it is said that General Vlastimir Djordjevic also attended this meeting, and Mr. Dragan Ilic, also a general.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Very briefly, Mr. Karleusa, could you indicate what was discussed according to the information available to the working group? What was discussed at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KARLEUSA
utterances.text: At that meeting, it was agreed how to carry out the instructions they had received at the office of then president Mr. Milosevic. And Mr. Vlajko Stojiljkovic gave Generals Djordjevic and Ilic the direct task of carrying this out.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Karleusa, was this information that the working group obtained, was that also made public in that -- in that communique?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KARLEUSA
utterances.text: It was not. I can't remember exactly. I don't think so. Perhaps it is actually there, but I really need to take a look here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Could I direct your attention, Mr. Karleusa, to the last page of tab 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Your Honours, that's the third paragraph, page 4 of tab 3 in English.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I can see it here. That's right. We did make it public.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Karleusa, in this paragraph and the paragraph above it, do these two paragraphs accurately reflect what your working group learned, or is it consistent with what the working group learned of these meetings?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KARLEUSA
utterances.text: Yes. According to the statement of Mr. Rade Markovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Karleusa, turning to the third meeting, when did that third meeting take place?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KARLEUSA
utterances.text: Somewhat later. It was held somewhat later. And there is an appropriate document concerning that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Who was present in that meeting according to the information the working group received?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KARLEUSA
utterances.text: General Djordjevic was present, General Dragan Ilic, and somebody else. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And was the subject matter at that meeting the same as the subject matters of the two other meetings?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KARLEUSA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Karleusa, could you please turn to tab 26. What is that document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KARLEUSA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Yes. Yes, tab 26. I'm sorry. Could you explain what that document is.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KARLEUSA
utterances.text: Lieutenant Slobodan Borisavljevic, at my request, gave a statement of his own. The statement was given on the 23rd of May, 2001. It says here that in the building of the city committee of the SPS in Belgrade, a meeting was held where General Djordjevic informed General Ilic that it was decided that on the territory of the Kosovo and Metohija the terrain was supposed to be cleared and that it was necessary to send expert assistance to our people in the field. For this assistance, he designated two police officers to go to Kosovo and to render assistance to the local organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Karleusa, we've heard the term "cleansing" in the cleaning of territory or of battlefield. That term in Serbian is, I believe, "asanacija." What is the ordinary meaning of that term, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KARLEUSA
utterances.text: As far as I know, "asanacija" is a normal term that means removing victims, casualties from the battlefield, human remains, livestock remains, chemical materials, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Based on the context in which your working group learned of this term as it was used in these three meetings, does that appear to you to be the meaning that term had in connection with those three meetings?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KARLEUSA
utterances.text: It seems that it was used in a different meaning.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'll just be a few more minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Karleusa, as far as you are aware, how did the public react to the work of the working group? If you could briefly describe that, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KARLEUSA
utterances.text: When the results obtained by the working group were made public, the public in Serbia became divided. May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Shin, you asked the witness if the term was used in the same way in those three meetings, and he said it seems to him that it was used in a different meaning. I think you should ask him what was that different meaning.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Karleusa, could you please explain your previous response when you say the term was used in a different meaning? Could you explain what you meant by that? What different meaning did it have? And we're referring to the term "cleansing," which is "asanacija" in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KARLEUSA
utterances.text: The very fact that according to the statement of Mr. Markovic, it was said that a removal of all traces should be carried out that might be subject of interest to The Hague Tribunal or, rather, that all bodies of civilians should either be dug up or found in some other way and transferred to a different locality means, as far as I'm concerned, it seems to me the term "asanacija," "clean-up," cannot be used in its regular, right meaning.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Karleusa, you were describing the reaction of the public to the work of the working group. Did you personally have any impact from the reaction of the public to the work of the working group?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KARLEUSA
utterances.text: Since the public has been divided in terms of their views on the results of the investigation carried out by the working group and that the majority of citizens know what this is about, but there is this other side that does not approve of this, I personally had negative experience in relation to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Could you very briefly specify what you mean by negative reaction.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KARLEUSA
utterances.text: Since I was the one presenting the findings of the working group to the public and, therefore, I appeared in public, I received several letters with threats, very serious threats, including death threats.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Karleusa, would you have attended to give evidence if you had not received the subpoena?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KARLEUSA
utterances.text: No, I would not have come.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I have no further questions. Your Honours, I offer the binder and the tabs within it, with the exception of tabs 1 and 2, into evidence in accordance with the decisions of the Trial Chamber earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. We've got an exhibit number for it which has already been given, so it's been admitted. Mr. Karleusa, if you'd be back, please, tomorrow morning for cross-examination. If you'd be back at 9.00, we'll go on then. Thank you. We will adjourn now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 23rd day of July, 2002, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.49 p.m.,
